chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him about a man who had two wives, and each of them bore him a son. Then one of his wives went and breastfed a girl from among the people. Is it appropriate for his son to marry this girl? He said: No, because she was breastfed with the milk of the old man.

key_terms.الشّيخ: the old man (referring to the husband)
key_terms.عُرضِ النّاس: among the people / from the general public

ai.seo_question: Does a wife's breastfeeding make the baby a milk sister to her husband's other children?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the mechanism of 'radhāʿah' (milk kinship) by establishing that the husband is considered the primary source of milk through his wife, thereby creating a permanent marital prohibition between him and the nursed child. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the attribution of milk to the male head of the household, ensuring that the son's right to marry the milk sister is preserved while the father's is barred.
